editorial:
Imagine finding a notebook that can kill anyone whose name you write inside it. That is the wild idea behind this 2017 crime fantasy thriller. You follow Light Turner, a smart but troubled teen who discovers the Death Note and starts using it to punish criminals. His actions draw the attention of L, a brilliant detective, Ryuk, a creepy demon who owns the book, and Mia, a classmate who becomes his partner in crime. The story mixes high school drama with supernatural thrills and a cat-and-mouse chase. The tone is dark, fast, and a little messy, but it keeps you watching to see who outsmarts who.

The acting is a mixed bag. Willem Dafoe's voice work as Ryuk is a standout, and Lakeith Stanfield brings energy to L. The pacing moves quickly, though some plot twists feel rushed. Pros include the cool concept and stylish visuals. Cons include thin character development and changes from the original manga that may upset fans. If you enjoy supernatural thrillers with a teen edge, give it a shot. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final act, Light and Mia ride a Ferris wheel while L closes in. Light reveals he hid Mia's name in the Death Note with a condition: she dies if she tries to kill him. When Mia attacks, she falls to her death. Light survives but is badly hurt. L cannot prove Light is Kira, though he suspects him. Ryuk appears and laughs at how humans turn on each other. The last scene hints Light still has a page of the notebook, suggesting his deadly game may not be over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural thrillers with a teen edge.
